root: ^Welcome to Wenchwatch Hall, sir. How might I be of assistance?

Start: ^I'm here to see the Admiral Charles Hold.
^I'm with the Weekly Wag! Here for the Admiral's big scoop!

c-0: ^Oh- I see. Was the Admiral- expecting you, sir?
^It's just- I wasn't aware of your visit.
^The Admiral invited me. I received this letter last night.
c-1: ^Oh, you're with the Weekly Wag! How thrilling! The Lady of the House is such a fan of your paper!
^But if you'll excuse me, sir- how have you already heard the news?
^The Admiral asked me to speak with him. I received this letter last night.
c-2: ^Dorothy Tendwell, sir. Lady's maid to Lady Theodosia Hold. How might I assist you?

Dorothy: ^Well, sir- I'm afraid you won't be able to speak with the Admiral today.
^Lady, I'm not leaving here without a story!
^I really must insist on seeing him. I won't get paid without a story.

c-0: ^Heavens, I'm not quite sure how to explain-
^Perhaps it's best you just see for yourself...
c-1: ^Well, seeing as you are so insistent I suppose it's best you see for yourself.
c-2: ^Well- if that is the case- perhaps it's best you see for yourself.

Body: ^As you can see sir, the Admiral is quite-
^Maximillian Hold, sir. Younger brother of the- late Admiral Charles Hold.
^Oh, dear brother! To be struck down so tragically!
^Ah! I do not know how my heart can bear such an onslaught of travesties!
^Oh- Dorothy dearest, who is this drably dressed fellow?
^This here is a journalist, sir. He says he's from the Weekly Wag.
^Ah! So the press have finally caught wind of my daring new fashion statement: Gloveless hands!
^I know what you're thinking! To expose one's hands to the elements, to the streets, to common folk! 'Tis a controversy in the making!
^But I assure you, six months from now, every man about town shall be following suit!
^I am not typically one for interviews, sir, being a terribly shy and private individual-
^But for you, mon chéri, I shall make an exception!
^Actually, I came here to speak to the Admiral.
^I don't care about your gloves! A man is dead!

c-2: ^Precisely, mon chéri! You clearly have a good sense of style, despite your hideous attire.

Theodosia_Enters: ^Sir Maximillian, it seems that the Admiral requested to speak to the gentleman here before his- departure.
^Apparently he had a story he felt important to share with the Weekly Wag- and the wider world.
^How enterprising of Charles to summon a newspaperman to Wenchwatch Hall in anticipation of his own murder.
^Such was the nature of my late husband- always a most forward-thinking fellow.
^Dorothy, I assure you, I am most well rested. One of the few benefits of widowhood is a night's sleep free of affectionate advances from one's husband.
^A pleasure to meet you, sir. I am an avid fan of your publication. Dorothy oft reads to me from its pages. I would read it myself, but female literacy is so terribly unfashionable at present.
^The exposé last month regarding Lady Sullivan's indecent table manners was particularly delectable.
^Most wonderful that you're here. One imagines you'll be taking my portraiture for your next issue, yes?
^The Admiral was murdered? Where is the killer?
^A murder? This is going to get me on the front page!

c-0: ^I'm afraid it's exactly as Lady Theodosia said, sir.
c-2: ^Sir, I would remine you that the Hold family are in mourning. I would suggest tempering your excitement.

Murder_Most_Foul: ^The Admiral was- struck down in the early hours of the morning by an unkown assailant. Worse yet, the body was discovered by the Admiral's son, little Avery Hold.
^The poor boy is traumatised. To discover your father in such a- after he-
^For heaven's sake, girl, pull yourself together! You should know how terribly gauche it is for servants to express sentiment.
^As I was saying, it was Avery who discovered the Admiral in his- current condition.
^Unfotunately, the killer escaped before Avery could catch sight of them.
Questioning: ^Everyone in Wenchwatch Hall last night is a suspect! Who was here last night?
^Has anyone questioned Avery in detail about what he saw?
^I'll solve this murder! I'll make sure the perpetrator is brought to justice!

c-0: ^There were five of us in total in Wenchwatch Hall last night, not including the Admiral.
^There was Sir Maximillian, who you have met-
^Lady Theodosia Hold, who you have also met-
^Theodosia stares at you, statuesque, as if preparing for her portrait.
^Not currently present is Avery Hold, the son of Lady Theodosia and the Admiral, and the stable hand, one Ms. Lavender Ditch.
^A most peculiar woman. To so enthusiastically spend one's days coated in horse manure - it defies all reason!
^Not to mention her general demeanour, dear Theodosia. So sullen- so uncouth!
^... Ms. Ditch likes to keep to herself. You will likely find her out in the stables tending to the horses.
c-1: ^The town constable has been alerted. But I'm afraid he's rather- idle- in his duties, and not known for having an eye for investigation.
^I very much doubt he'll be capable of tracking down the killer...
c-2: ^I found Avery standing over the Admiral just before sunrise- hardly three hours ago. I didn't think it proper to further traumatise the poor child.
c-3: ^I am quite sure there is nothing on this Earth Charles would want more than to be prominently featured in a paper of note. Dead or no.

Outro: ^If you are quite set on helping us, sir, I shall make sure everyone remains at Wenchwatch Hall as you carry out your investigation.
^I would recommend you carry out a thorough investigation of the Admiral's- ahem- body-
^It might help you with your investigation.
